newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower, graft scandal hits.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower, graft scandal hits.

text.p: Stocks ended sharply lower on Friday as the already fragile market sentiment was affected by the government's plan to sell Korea Telecom shares, brokers said.
A bribery scandal involving the president of a leading commercial bank also affected the overall mood, they said.
The composite index was down 1.81 percent, or 13.45 points to a provisional close of 731.46.
"It's hard to blame any one specific factor for today's fall, but a longstanding mix of factors and the lack of good news were to blame," said Kim Heung-shik of Hyundai Securities.
Losers overwhelmed gainers 706 to 182. Volume totalled a low 24.23 million shares.
The state Korean Broadcasting System reported that the president of SEOULBANK was under investigation on charges of taking kickbacks from companies in return for loans.
The bank officially denied the reports and prosecution officials declined to comment. SEOULBANK closed at 4,600 won, up 30 won on the day after falling to this year's lowest level of 4,450.
"Investors were concerned that the scandal could affect the already unstable money market," said an LG Securities broker.
Sammi Steel and Sammi Corp, both flagship units of Sammi Group, fell sharply on rumours that the group was suffering from financial difficulties. A group spokesman denied the rumours.
Both closed at their daily lower limits. Sammi Steel fell 250 won to 4,070 and Sammi Corp down 190 won to 3,010.

Mirae Corp, a semiconductor inspection equipment maker, ended its first day of public trading at its daily upper limit. It gained 4,200 won to 74,200. But none of the Mirae shares changed hands as no holders of the shares was willing to sell.
Wooshin Industries, which also newly listed its shares, gained 2,400 won to end at its limit of 42,400.
Two other newly listed shares ended at their daily lower limits. Dong Won Fisheries was down 700 won to 12,300 and Kohap Petrochemical shed 900 won to 14,100.
The four newly listed shares traded only during the morning session. The exchange said the step was to ensure that the computer systems were not overwhelmed by orders.
The December futures contracts ended 1.25 points lower at 77.40 while the KOSPI-200 index shed 1.44 points to 76.76.
The exchange later revised the day's closing index to 731.44, down 13.47 points on the day.
